did_you_know.text: Did you know? The battle between the Philistines and Israel took place on Mount Gilboa. Israel was defeated, and many soldiers were killed.
Did you know? The three sons of Saul who were killed in the battle were Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
Did you know? Saul was severely wounded by the archers, and the text emphasizes that he suffered greatly from them.

Did you know? Saul asked his armor-bearer to kill him so that he would not fall into the hands of the Philistines and be abused by them. But his armor-bearer was afraid and refused, so Saul fell on his own sword.
Did you know? When Saul’s armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell on his own sword and died with his king.
Did you know? That same day, Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer, and other men from the army of Israel died.

Did you know? When the Israelites in the valley and east of the Jordan heard about Israel’s defeat and the deaths of Saul and his sons, they abandoned their cities, and the Philistines settled in them.
Did you know? It was not until the day after the battle that the Philistines came to strip the bodies of the fallen. That was when they found Saul and his three sons who had fallen on Mount Gilboa.
Did you know? The Philistines cut off Saul’s head, stripped off his armor, and sent the news throughout their land to publicize their victory.
Did you know? Saul’s armor was placed in the temple of the Ashtoreths, and his body was displayed on the wall of Beth-shean.
Did you know? When the people of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul, they set out during the night to recover the bodies of Saul and his sons.
Did you know? The people of Jabesh-gilead traveled all night, brought the bodies to Jabesh, burned them there, and then buried the bones beneath the tamarisk tree.
Did you know? After the burial, the people of Jabesh-gilead fasted for seven days as a sign of mourning and respect for Saul and his sons.
